newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS-EU raids firms in amino-acid price probe.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-EU raids firms in amino-acid price probe.

text.p: The European Commission said on Thursday it was investigating a number of non-EU companies, including U.S. agribusiness giant ADM Co, over price fixing allegations involving amino acids used in animal feed.
Dawn raids were made at the European headquarters of the companies in Germany and Britain on Wednesday. They were continuing on Thursday when a Commission spokesman confirmed the investigation.

"I can confirm our inspectors have been conducting (raids) at the European headquarters of a series of companies...our inspectors are still around, apparently in Germany and the United Kingdom," an EU spokesman said.
He confirmed that ADM was being investigated as the company said on Wednesday but declined to name the other firms involved.

Another EU source said later that three companies were being investigated, including Archer Daniels Midland Co (ADM), and that they were all based outside the 15-nation European Union but had operations in Europe.

ADM, which pleaded guilty to price-fixing charges in the U.S. last year, said on Wednesday it and several of its European subsidiaries were among the targets of an anti-competitive practices probe by the Commission.

The U.S. agricultural products processor said in a statement the Commission was probing the possible participation of major manufacturers in anti-competitive practices or agreements in certain EU markets for amino acids, including the feed additive lysine.

EU sources confirmed lysine was one and probably the main product concerned. They said the European market for the product, used in pig and poultry, was worth an annual 250 million European currency units ($282 million).
They said that competitors had complained about alleged price-fixing, but declined to give names. They added that some companies were cooperating with the EU's competition officials.
ADM pleaded guilty in the U.S. last year to fixing prices of lysine and the food additive citric acid, and paid a record $100 million in fines.
The U.S. Justice Department probe also resulted in charges against Ajinimoto Co Inc and Kyowa Hakko Kogyo Co Ltd of Japan and Sewon America Inc.
ADM said the Commission probe was in its early stages and the outcome could not be predicted.
The Commission can fine firms found guilty of colluding on market share or price rigging up to 10 percent of their annual turnover, depending on the offences and how long they last. ($1 = 0.885 Ecus)
